How to do itKettlebell Swing

Top position

Right
STANDING TALL
Wrong
LEANING BACK

Right: Standing tall, ankles, knees, hips and shoulders in line.

Wrong: Leaning back at the top.

Back shape

Right
BACK FLAT
Wrong
BACK ROUNDED

Right: Back flat, hips pushed back.

Wrong: Lower back rounded.

Hips back, knees only slightly bent.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Leaning backLeaning back at the top of the swing.
  2. Low back archesThe low back overextends instead of the glutes finishing.
Drive1 s
Swing down1 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your glutes and the backs of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansYou are lifting with the arms instead of the hips.

    FixDrive with your hips. Keep your arms straight and loose.

  • Usually meansA crush grip can stress them.

    FixGrip firmly, not too tightly: an easy hook grip.

  • Usually meansYour form may be breaking down.

    FixStop or reset your form.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet about shoulder-width and planted, the bell a foot in front.

  2. 2

    Hinge and grip, palms down side by side, bell tilted toward you.

  3. 3

    Hike it high between your legs, then swing to about chest height.

  4. 4

    Don't hold your breath: out as it rises, in as it falls.

  5. 5

    Keep a full grip. Set the bell on the ground when done.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rounding the lower back strains it.
  • Leaning back at the top puts more pressure on the lower back.
  • A loose grip could let the bell slip or be dropped.

Back pain

How to do itHigh Knees

Knee height

Right
THIGH TO HIP
Wrong
BACK ARCHED

Right: Thigh at about hip height, chest tall.

Wrong: Knee driven higher, lower back arched.

Stand tall, eyes ahead, core braced.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back archesThe lower back arches and the trunk tips back.
  2. Knee too highThe knee is driven so high that the lower back arches.
Work30 s
Rest30 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your hips and thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The trunk braces to keep you balanced as the legs switch.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand tall, feet about hip-width apart, arms at your sides.

  2. 2

    Brace your trunk, shift onto the balls of your feet, knees soft.

  3. 3

    Drive one knee to hip height as the opposite arm pumps up.

  4. 4

    Lower it quickly and switch legs.

  5. 5

    To start, work 30 seconds, then rest 30 seconds.

Risks and when to stop

  • Driving the knees too high arches the lower back.
  • Wear supportive shoes. Knee or ankle issues? Use a gym floor or grass.
  • Knee height dropping, or legs turning out more as you tire? Take a rest.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itJump Rope

Hop height

Right
LOW HOP
Wrong
TOO HIGH

Right: Soft knees, landing softly on the balls of the feet.

Wrong: Jumping too high over the rope.

Elbow position

Right
ELBOWS IN
Wrong

Right: Elbows close to the ribs, hands by the hips.

Wrong: Shoulders swinging, elbows out wide.

Elbows stay close to your ribs.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Too highJumping far higher than the rope needs.
Work30 s
Rest60 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your calves and the front of your thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansFeeling the turn here means it starts in the wrong place.

    FixTurn the rope with your wrists, elbows in.

  • Usually meansAn ache here usually comes from the arms turning the rope.

    FixKeep your elbows close to your ribs. Turn the rope with your wrists.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand on the rope's middle. The handles should reach your armpits.

  2. 2

    Hold the handles loosely, toward their ends. White knuckles are too tight.

  3. 3

    Feet together, rope behind your feet, hands by your sides.

  4. 4

    Swing it overhead and hop about 1 to 2 inches each turn.

  5. 5

    Where possible, avoid concrete. A sprung wooden or matted floor is better.

Risks and when to stop

  • Turning the rope with your arms, not your wrists, can make your wrists hurt.
  • Too much too soon can leave your feet and shins sore.
  • Check overhead: hitting a light or ceiling fan could cause serious injury.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

Shoulder blades

Knees slightly bent, back straight, a slight forward lean.

Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your front shoulders, sides of the waist and forearms.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The trunk works with the obliques and low back.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansShoulder blades lifting or hunching forward strains the neck.

    FixSlide your shoulder blades down and back.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Feet planted hip-width apart, a little slack in the ropes.

  2. 2

    Handshake grip on each rope end.

  3. 3

    Bend your knees slightly and lean forward a little, back straight.

  4. 4

    Shoulders back, trunk braced. Don't hold your breath as you speed up.

  5. 5

    Arms in front, swing one rope up as the other comes down.

Risks and when to stop

  • Lifted or hunched shoulder blades strain the neck.
  • Adding speed or a heavier rope too soon? Get the form right first.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itSled Pull

Torso stack

Right
OVER HIPS
Wrong
PITCHED BACK

Right: Shoulders over hips in a quarter squat.

Wrong: Torso pitched back, lower back loaded.

Knees soft in a quarter squat, chest up, core braced.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Torso pitched backThe torso pitches back and the lower back takes the load.
  2. Shoulders behind hipsThe shoulders are no longer over the hips, leaning too far back.
WalkQuick
Look closer

Grip

Both hands on the rope, one over the other.

Keep your wrists firm and your elbows tucked.

Common handling mistakes

  • Leaning back

    Fix: Keep your torso braced, shoulders over hips. Go lighter.

  • Yanking with the arms

    Fix: Lead with your legs.

  • Rope piled at your feet

    Fix: Flick or step it aside between steps.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in the front of your thighs and your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The trunk stays braced so the torso stays tall.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansTorso pitched back, lower back taking the load.

    FixBrace, keep shoulders over hips, and use a lighter sled.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Face the sled, rope in both hands, one hand over the other.

  2. 2

    Step back for light tension in the rope. Chin level, eyes forward.

  3. 3

    Feet shoulder-width, sink into a quarter squat, chest up, trunk braced.

  4. 4

    Step back one foot at a time, short and quick.

  5. 5

    Feed the rope through your hands. Flick the piled rope aside.

Risks and when to stop

  • Leaning back puts the load on your lower back.
  • Slack rope at your feet can trip you.
  • A rounded back can strain your lower spine.

Right: Soft landing, knees slightly bent.

Wrong: Hard landing, knees not bent.

Saved offline
Tells

Squat downControlled
Kick back 
Jump in 
Jump up 
Look closer

Grip

Hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rushing the transitions

    Fix: Control your movements.

  • Hard landing on the jump

    Fix: Land softly on slightly bent knees.

  • Lower back sagging

    Fix: Brace your trunk. Keep your body straight from head to heels.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your chest, the front of your thighs and your glutes.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA hard landing: the impact could hurt them.

    FixLand softly on slightly bent knees. Stop if pain occurs.

  • Usually meansDiving onto your hands may hurt your wrists.

    FixPlace your hands on the floor first. Stop if you feel pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart. Don't hold your breath.

  2. 2

    Squat down. Hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.

  3. 3

    Hands down first, then kick your feet back into a plank.

  4. 4

    Lower your chest to the floor, neck neutral, then push back up.

  5. 5

    Jump your feet under you, knees over toes, then jump up.

Risks and when to stop

  • Landing on straight knees, the impact could hurt feet, ankles, knees, hips or back.
  • Diving onto your hands may hurt your wrists.
  • Rushing the transitions can stress your joints.

Knee pain

Severe pain, badly swollen, changed shape, locking, giving way, or can't put weight on it? Get it checked today.

No better after a few weeks? See a doctor.

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

How to do itBear Crawl

Hip line

Right
HIPS LEVEL
Wrong

Right: Hips level with the shoulders, back flat.

Wrong: Hips raised above the back.

Palms pressed into the floor, hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips.

Tells
  1. Hips riseThe hips rise above the line of the back as the knees lift.
  2. Hips above shouldersThe hips sit higher than the shoulders.
Work15–30 s
Look closer

Grip

Palm pressed into the floor, hand under the shoulder.

Common handling mistakes

  • Hips rise as you crawl

    Fix: Keep hips in line with the back. Bear plank until you can.

  • Back arches

    Fix: Tighten your trunk.

  • Hips sway side to side

    Fix: Take shorter steps.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your belly and sides, shoulders and front thighs.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

The core holds the whole body steady.

If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansWith this pain under load, scans often find a wrist problem.

    FixCheck the wrist box below.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Get on hands and knees: hands under shoulders, knees under hips.

  2. 2

    Press palms into the floor, brace, lift knees about 2 inches.

  3. 3

    Move one hand and the opposite foot forward, then switch.

  4. 4

    Keep your back straight and your hips level with your shoulders.

  5. 5

    One drill is 4 steps forward, then 4 steps back.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pain on the back of the wrist in the loaded, bent-back position.
  • An arched back can be painful.

Wrist pain

Can't grip, wrist changed shape, or hand gone numb? Get it checked today.

Tingling, keeps coming back, or no better after two weeks' rest? See a doctor.

Flat back

Right

Right: Back flat, head to hips in a straight line.

Wrong: Back rounded.

Right

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Back roundsThe back rounds instead of staying flat.

Walk 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs, glutes and calves.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA rounded back.

    FixHinge at your hips and keep your back flat.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Load the sled. Check the path is flat and clear.

  2. 2

    Stand behind the sled. Hands about halfway down the handles, arms straight.

  3. 3

    Step back and lean forward, head to hips in a straight line.

  4. 4

    Keep arms straight the whole push, shoulders behind your hands.

  5. 5

    Tighten your abs, spine neutral, eyes just ahead of the sled.

Risks and when to stop

  • Pushing with a rounded back is not good for your spine.
  • Bent arms may cause some discomfort in your elbows and shoulders.
  • Hips rising or chest dropping as you tire? Keep the same body angle.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your abs and lats.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansRounding the back as you slam or pick up the ball.

    FixKeep your back flat and hinge from the hips.

Set it up

  1. 1

  2. 2

How to do itFarmer's Carry

Shoulders down

Right
BACK AND DOWN
Wrong
SHRUGGED HIGH

Right: Shoulders back and down.

Wrong: Shoulders shrugged high.

Tall torso

Right
TALL
Wrong
LEANING FORWARD

Right: Tall and upright, arms long, weights even.

Wrong: Leaning forward.

Torso upright and chest tall, gaze ahead.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Steps too longA regular-sized step, too long for a beginner.
WalkControlled
Look closer

Grip

Palm pushed into the handle, thumb wrapped, fingers curled around it. Not in the fingers only.

Common handling mistakes

  • Rushing the walk

    Fix: Don't rush for distance. Turn in small steps, not a sharp pivot.

  • Steps too long

    Fix: Take short, deliberate steps. Steps out of control? End the carry.

  • Shrugging as you tire

    Fix: Keep your shoulders back and down. Posture changing? End the carry.

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your forearms and traps.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansA handle starts slipping.

    FixEnd the carry. Bend your hips and knees, lower the weights beside you, feet clear.

  • Usually meansNot bracing your trunk.

    FixBrace before you lift. Stop if you feel pain.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Clear a level, dry route, with room to set down.

  2. 2

    Stand between the weights, feet about hip-width apart.

  3. 3

    Bend at your hips and knees and grip, thumbs wrapped.

  4. 4

    Breathe in, brace, and stand up without jerking the weights.

  5. 5

    Stand fully tall, arms long at your sides, before your first step.

Risks and when to stop

  • Rushing: one misstep could pull a calf, roll an ankle or twist a knee.
  • Not bracing can wreak havoc on your lower back.
  • Without a good grip, the weights may slip and land on your toe.

How to do itJumping Jacks

Toes forward

Right
TOES FORWARD
Wrong
TOES OUT

Right: Toes pointed forward.

Wrong: Toes twisted outward.

Land with a slight bend in the knees, never locked.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Toes outThe toes twist outward instead of pointing forward.
Work30–60 s
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs, glutes and shoulders.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt

Set it up

  1. 1

    Use flat, even ground. Rubber or grass absorbs shock better than concrete.

  2. 2

    Stand with your feet together and your arms at your sides.

  3. 3

    Jump your feet apart as your arms go overhead.

  4. 4

    Land softly, knees slightly bent.

  5. 5

    Jump back together as your arms come down, and go again.

Risks and when to stop

  • Stiff-kneed landings add joint stress. Jerky landings add impact stress.
  • Hard surfaces like cement absorb less shock than rubber or grass.
  • Rushing the reps can lead to overuse injuries. Choose a suitable speed.

General guidance, not medical advice. If something hurts, stop and get it checked.

How to do itWall Ball

Wall distance

Right
ARM'S LENGTH
Wrong
TOO FAR BACK

Right: Arms out, the ball touches the wall.

Wrong: Too far back: the ball goes forward, body tilts.

Arms out, the ball touches the wall: stand there.

Saved offline
Tells
  1. Too farThe feet stand too far from the wall.
  2. Body tilts forwardThe body tilts forward to reach the wall.
Squat 
Throw 
Look closer

Where you should feel it

You should feel this in your thighs, glutes, shoulders and upper chest.

MainAlso workingShould not take overWhere it may hurt
If you feel it in…

  • Usually meansThe right distance from the wall takes strain off them.

    FixHold your arms out, ball touching the wall: stand there.

Set it up

  1. 1

    Face a sturdy wall at arm's length, feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out.

  2. 2

    Brace and stand tall, ball close at chest height, elbows tucked in.

  3. 3

    Breathe in, squat: weight in heels, chest up, thighs parallel or lower.

  4. 4

    Breathe out, drive up through your heels and throw to the target.

  5. 5

    Catch tall, hands under the ball, elbows high, not sandwiching it.

Risks and when to stop

  • Catching at the bottom of the squat makes the impact feel heavier.
  • Too close to the wall, the ball will probably fall on your face.
  • Tired arms can let the ball smash into your face.

Shoulder pain

Sudden or severe, after falling, or arm won't move? Get it checked today.

Getting worse, very hard to move, or no better after two weeks? See a doctor.
